title: Top K Frequent Elements
kidExplanation: Numbers shout how often they appear. You only want the k loudest voices on the podium.
plainProblem: Return the k most frequent elements in the array. Order among the top-k does not matter.

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: Count frequencies, sort all unique numbers by count, take k.

thinkingSteps.title: Why sorting works
thinkingSteps.body: Simple, O(m log m) for m unique values.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: Bucket sort by frequency: index = count, values = numbers with that count.

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
thinkingSteps.body: Fill frequency buckets, then walk from high frequency down until you collect k numbers.

pattern.name: Hash set / hash map for seen items
pattern.whenToSpot: You need fast lookups of values you already saw.

complexity.timeReason: Counting is O(n); bucket walk is O(n) because total bucket entries equal n.
complexity.spaceReason: Frequency map and buckets store up to n items.

edgeCases: Duplicates and boundary values from the constraints.
commonMistakes: Coding before stating the pattern and complexity.
Off-by-one errors on indices or window edges.
Mutating data structures while iterating carelessly.
interviewTips: Name the pattern: Hash set / hash map for seen items.
State O(n) time and O(n) space at the end.

interviewApproachNotes: Bucket sort by frequency is the NeetCode favorite and impresses more than sorting when you explain why it is linear. Heap of size k is also acceptable O(n log k).
